sections.title: Virginia rose
sections.text: An upright, suckering shrub native to eastern North America. It typically grows about 1.2–1.8 m tall, with compound leaves and prickly canes. Its five-petalled pink flowers are followed by round, bright-red hips, about 1 cm wide.

sections.title: Fruit and comparison
sections.text: North Carolina Extension lists the ripe hips as edible. Remove the seed hairs when preparing them; those hairs can irritate the mouth and gut. The species is a compact North American shrub, unlike the longer, scrambling stems and dense white flower clusters of Rosa multiflora.
